note: Bends checked by ear: the target note played first, then the bend held against a drone, then a second bend on the B string that ends on the drone's own note, used in the learner's phrases. One minor pentatonic position on the screen, so no number; the key moves (any key) and is named only as {{=key}}, each block's tools sit inside it (its own drone), and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: Bends in tune
exercise.why: A bend is in tune when it reaches the sound of the note two frets up, so play that note first, then bend until you match it.

cells.text:
The neck below holds the notes of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale, a little up the neck. On the G string, play the ringed {{5}} and keep its sound in your ear. Then bend {{4}}, the note under it on the same string, up until it sounds the same.
Practice until the bend stops on the sound of {{5}} without you checking.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. Bend {{4}} up to {{5}} again and hold it at the top.
Listen for the bend to arrive: the held note and the drone sound steady together, and while the bend is short they beat against each other.

Press Play below to start the drone. On the B string, play the ringed {{1}}, then bend {{b7}} up to it: this bend ends on the drone's own note, so you hear it settle.
Then make up short phrases that end on one of the two bends.
{{?key}}In another key the position sits on other frets, and both bends still go up two frets on the same strings.
